title: Vibrations on String

description: Investigate the relationship between tension, frequency and wavelength of a vibrating string.

precautions.title: 🎯 Resonance Tension & String Snap Hazard
precautions.description: Keep faces away from the plane of the vibrating string. High tensile loading combined with harmonic resonance can cause snapping.

theory.title: 📖 Theory — Transverse Vibrations on a Stretched String
theory.objective: To investigate standing wave phenomena in stretched strings, verify the dependency of wave speed on tension and linear mass density, and confirm Melde's frequency and harmonic relations.
points: A transverse mechanical wave propagating along a flexible stretched string reflects at the fixed boundaries with an inverted phase (180° phase shift).

Superposition of the incident wave and reflected wave produces a standing wave pattern characterized by stationary points of zero motion (nodes) and alternating points of maximum oscillation (antinodes).
Boundary conditions require nodes at both clamped ends (x = 0 and x = L), restricting sustainable vibrations to discrete harmonic modes n = 1, 2, 3...
Increasing string tension increases the restoring force, speeding up wave propagation and shifting natural resonant frequencies higher.

formulaDetails.name: Transverse Wave Propagation Velocity

variables.name: Wave Velocity
variables.desc: Phase speed at which transverse disturbances travel down the string

variables.name: String Tension
variables.desc: Tensile stretching force applied to string (T = m_suspended · g)

variables.name: Linear Mass Density
variables.desc: Mass per unit length of string material (μ = m_string / L_string)

formulaDetails.description: Wave speed depends exclusively on the balance between restoring tension (T) and inertial mass per unit length (μ). Higher tension increases speed, while heavier cords slow it down.
formulaDetails.physicalSignificance: Directly tested in the laboratory by changing slotted weights suspended over the end pulley.

formulaDetails.name: Standing Wave Harmonic Resonant Frequency

variables.name: Resonant Frequency
variables.desc: Frequency required to sustain the n-th standing harmonic mode

variables.name: Harmonic Mode Number
variables.desc: Number of vibrating loops (half-wavelength segments) between boundaries

variables.name: Vibrating String Length
variables.desc: Clear distance between the mechanical oscillator tip and the pulley

formulaDetails.description: Standing wave condition demands that the length of the string must accommodate an integer number of half-wavelengths: L = n · (λ / 2).
formulaDetails.physicalSignificance: Fundamental mode (n = 1) forms a single central antinode. Higher harmonics (n = 2, 3...) produce multiple distinct loops separated by stationary nodes.

formulaDetails.name: Harmonic Wavelength Relation

variables.name: Wavelength of Mode n
variables.desc: Spatial distance spanning one complete sinusoidal wave cycle (two full loops)

variables.name: Harmonic Mode
variables.desc: Total loop count observed along string span

formulaDetails.description: The physical distance between two consecutive nodes is exactly half a wavelength (λ / 2). Thus, measuring the distance between adjacent nodes provides an accurate measure of λ.
formulaDetails.physicalSignificance: Enables students to determine wave speed experimentally without requiring high-speed stroboscopic motion tracking.

formulaDetails.name: Standing Wave Profile Equation
formulaDetails.formula: y(x, t) = 2A · sin((n · π · x) / L) · cos(2π · f_n · t)

variables.name: Transverse Displacement
variables.desc: Vertical deflection of a string element at position x and time t

variables.name: Incident Amplitude
variables.desc: Peak amplitude of individual component traveling waves

variables.name: Longitudinal Coordinate
variables.desc: Position along string axis from clamped boundary

formulaDetails.description: Expresses standing wave motion as the product of a pure spatial shape factor sin(nπx/L) and a temporal oscillation cos(ωt). At nodes (sin = 0), displacement remains zero at all times.
formulaDetails.physicalSignificance: Explains why nodes never move and why energy is trapped between boundaries rather than flowing along the wire.
